responseText: I’m treating these as fixed constraints: clean-room implementation, graph/layer workflow, SQLite-backed asset/provenance catalog, reusable primitives, and post-production text/captions rather than model-rendered text. Your uploaded handoff also frames Arcads as a model-router plus project/asset/template/workflow system, not one magic model. api-openapi-summary source-digest README video-creative-direction One important current provider caveat: do not make OpenAI Sora the foundation of this build. The OpenAI Videos API / Sora 2 docs currently say Sora 2 and Sora 2 Pro are deprecated and scheduled to shut down on September 24, 2026; it is still useful as a compatibility adapter, but not as your stable production backbone. OpenAI Developers+1 Executive architecture opinion Build this as a local-first creative operating system: Product / inspiration input→ normalized assets→ format decomposition→ graph recipe→ node execution→ asset catalog writes→ deterministic render→ scoring + remix loop Do not start with a SaaS-like “generate ad” button. That is the trap. Start with: A typed graph runner. A SQLite asset/provenance catalog. A provider router. A deterministic Remotion/ffmpeg renderer. A small set of UGC recipes that can produce 3–5 variants. The Arcads-like surface emerges from repeatable recipes, reusable assets, and batch orchestration. 1. Proposed architecture Packages/apps to add Core packages packages/ugc-core Shared domain types: Asset, Product, Persona, Voice, Script, Shot, Caption, WorkflowGraph, TimelineLayer, NodeRun, ProviderJob. packages/asset-catalog SQLite catalog, migrations, asset hashing, sidecar metadata, provenance writes, tag/vibe indexing, asset lookup, derived-asset relationships. Use Bun’s built-in bun:sqlite first; Bun documents native SQLite support through bun:sqlite, which fits your “avoid native modules unless isolated” preference. Bun packages/graph-runner DAG executor with node contracts, cache keys, retries, dependency resolution, artifact writes, and “resume from failed node.” packages/provider-router Capability-based provider abstraction: llm.planllm.extractimage.generateimage.editvideo.t2vvideo.i2vvideo.v2vvideo.extendtts.generatevoice.cloneasr.transcribetranslate.textlipsync.generatesegment.maskrender.composeanalyze.creative Provider adapters should be dumb. Routing logic belongs in provider-router, not in every recipe. packages/video-renderer Remotion compositions, ffmpeg helpers, ASS/SRT subtitle utilities, audio normalization, concat, crop/pad, watermark/debug overlays, thumbnails. Remotion is a good fit because it lets you build reusable, parameterized video templates with props; ffmpeg stays as the lower-level normalization/transcode/filter workhorse. FFmpeg+3Remotion+3Remotion+3 packages/product-ingest Product URL/page/image ingestion using your existing packages/web-access: fetch, browser session, screenshots, image extraction, metadata extraction, LLM normalization. For commodity fallback, Firecrawl, Browserbase, Jina Reader, and Mozilla Readability are good optional adapters: Firecrawl is positioned as an API for search/scrape/structured web data, Browserbase supports Playwright cloud browser sessions, Jina Reader converts URLs to LLM-ready Markdown, and Mozilla Readability is an npm-available standalone article parser. GitHub+3Firecrawl+3docs.browserbase.com+3 packages/format-decomposer Reference video/slideshow decomposition: scene cuts, transcript, beat timing, caption style extraction, shot rhythm, hook taxonomy, product/demo/proof/CTA slots. packages/workflow-recipes YAML/JSON recipes and Zod schemas: ugc-product-demo-v0.yamltalking-head-broll-v0.yamlslideshow-ad-v0.yamlapp-demo-ugc-v0.yamlunboxing-pov-v0.yamlactor-swap-experiment-v0.yaml packages/analysis-loop LLM and rules-based creative scoring, human review forms, metric imports, remix recommendations. Apps apps/ugc-cli Main Bun CLI: Bashbun run ugc product ingest ...bun run ugc recipe create ...bun run ugc run ...bun run ugc render ...bun run ugc assets search ... apps/ugc-worker Queue worker for provider jobs, local render jobs, retries, and future GPU dispatch. For the first 48 hours, use a SQLite-backed queue table. For v1, BullMQ + Redis is the pragmatic upgrade because BullMQ is a Redis-backed queue available for Node.js/Bun and built for background job processing. BullMQ+1 apps/ugc-studio Editor-lite/workflow-lite UI: React/ViteReact Flow graph canvasRemotion Player previewAsset browserRun inspectorPrompt/provenance panelVariant table apps/asset-browser Can be merged into ugc-studio, but initially a simple asset viewer is useful. Isolated local/GPU services services/comfy-bridge HTTP bridge to ComfyUI on the RTX 3090 machine. Keep Python/native GPU mess isolated. The Bun monorepo talks to it over HTTP. services/lipsync-worker Optional Python worker for MuseTalk/Wav2Lip/SadTalker/LivePortrait if you do not use Fal/Replicate. services/ffmpeg-worker Optional later if render jobs become heavy. Local data directories data/ asset-catalog/ assets.sqlite migrations/ projects/ <project_slug>/ project.json products/ raw/ normalized/ inputs/ uploads/ urls/ reference-videos/ recipes/ ugc-product-demo-v0.yaml runs/ <run_id>/ graph.json manifest.json cost.json node-runs/ <node_id>.request.json <node_id>.response.json <node_id>.log assets/ generated/ derived/ temp/ renders/ variant-001.mp4 variant-002.mp4 thumbs/ exports/ mp4/ captions/ manifests/ assets/ raw/ uploads/ generated/ images/ videos/ audio/ derived/ masks/ thumbnails/ captions/ transcripts/ waveforms/ providers/ requests/ responses/ webhooks/ templates/ formats/ caption-styles/ personas/ render-styles/ Make the asset catalog source of truth; filesystem paths are just storage locations. SQLite schema concepts Use SQL migrations, not ORM magic at first. created_at TEXT NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY(parent_asset_id) REFERENCES assets(id), FOREIGN KEY(child_asset_id) REFERENCES assets(id), FOREIGN KEY(node_run_id) REFERENCES node_runs(id));CREATE TABLE analysis_scores ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, asset_id TEXT, run_id TEXT, scorer TEXT NOT NULL, -- human, llm, heuristic, platform_metric score_type TEXT NOT NULL, -- hook, clarity, scroll_stop, cringe, proof, brand_fit, caption_safety score REAL NOT NULL, notes TEXT, metadata_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', created_at TEXT NOT NULL); Later additions: sqlite-vec or external embeddings for semantic asset search, but do not block MVP on vector search. Job queue/orchestration 48-hour version Use a table: SQLCREATE TABLE jobs ( id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, queue TEXT NOT NULL, type TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, priority INTEGER DEFAULT 0, attempts INTEGER DEFAULT 0, max_attempts INTEGER DEFAULT 3, payload_json TEXT NOT NULL, result_json TEXT, locked_by TEXT, locked_at TEXT, run_after TEXT, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL, error TEXT); A Bun worker polls: queued → running → succeeded/failed This is enough for local prototyping. v1 version Use BullMQ + Redis for execution state, but still write canonical run state to SQLite: SQLite = truthBullMQ = work dispatchFilesystem = asset bytesProvider logs = reproducibility/debugging Do not let Redis become the product database. Provider abstraction Provider routing should use capability keys, not hardcoded product names: TypeScriptexport type ProviderCapability = | "llm.plan" | "llm.extract" | "image.generate" | "image.edit" | "video.t2v" | "video.i2v" | "video.v2v" | "video.extend" | "tts.generate" | "voice.clone" | "asr.transcribe" | "translate.text" | "lipsync.generate" | "segment.mask" | "render.compose" | "analyze.creative";export interface ProviderRequest<TParams = unknown> { capability: ProviderCapability; provider: string; model?: string; inputAssets?: string[]; prompt?: string; params: TParams; cache?: { enabled: boolean; keyParts: unknown[]; };}export interface ProviderResult<TOutput = unknown> { output: TOutput; assets?: NewAssetRecord[]; rawRequest?: unknown; rawResponse?: unknown; costUsd?: number; latencyMs?: number; providerJobId?: string;} Provider adapters to add first: OpenAIProvider llm, image, tts, asr, optional/deprecated videoAnthropicProvider llm planning, decomposition, critiqueGeminiProvider llm, image/Nano Banana, Veo video, TTS where usefulJimengProvider image/video via existing packageFalProvider video/image/lipsync/open modelsReplicateProvider open model fallback + experimentsElevenLabsProvider TTS/voice cloneCartesiaProvider fast TTS/voice cloneRunwayProvider video generation/editingKlingProvider video generation/editing if direct API accessLocalComfyProvider local RTX 3090 workflowsFFmpegProvider normalize, concat, subtitle, transcodeRemotionProvider deterministic composition Google’s Gemini API currently exposes Nano Banana image generation/editing and Veo 3.1 video generation; the Veo docs specifically call out up to three reference images for preserving people/characters/products. Google AI for Developers+2Google AI for Developers+2 Rendering/compositing Use timeline layers, not “one video blob.” TypeScripttype TimelineLayer = | { type: "video"; assetId: string; startMs: number; endMs: number; fit: "cover" | "contain"; transform?: Transform } | { type: "image"; assetId: string; startMs: number; endMs: number; transform?: Transform } | { type: "audio"; assetId: string; startMs: number; volume?: number; ducking?: boolean } | { type: "caption"; captionAssetId: string; styleId: string; startMs: number; endMs: number } | { type: "text"; text: string; startMs: number; endMs: number; styleId: string } | { type: "effect"; effectId: string; startMs: number; endMs: number; params: Record<string, unknown> }; Recommended render path: 1. Normalize all generated clips to 1080x1920, 30fps, h264 mezzanine.2. Generate word-level captions from final audio.3. Compose in Remotion: - talking head layer - b-roll/product/app layers - product overlay - captions - CTA text - debug/provenance overlay when requested4. Export mp4.5. ffmpeg pass: - loudnorm - final bitrate - faststart - thumbnail Use ffmpeg drawtext/ASS only for simpler CLI fallback; use Remotion for editor-lite because captions, kinetic typography, app screens, and split layouts are easier as React components. Workflow graph format A workflow has two parts: DAG nodes: produce assets/JSON. Timeline layers: final edit decision list. Example: YAMLid: ugc-product-demo-v0version: 0.1.0defaults: aspect: "9:16" width: 1080 height: 1920 fps: 30 language: en durationTargetSec: 28inputs: productUrl: type: string productImage: type: asset? variants: type: number default: 5nodes: product: type: product.ingest inputs: url: "{{inputs.productUrl}}" image: "{{inputs.productImage}}" scripts: type: script.generateVariants dependsOn: [product] params: count: "{{inputs.variants}}" format: "problem-solution-proof-cta" maxWords: 72 persona: type: persona.selectOrGenerate dependsOn: [product] params: archetype: "selfie_ugc_creator" count: "{{inputs.variants}}" diversity: ["age", "style", "room", "energy"] avoidRealPersonClone: true voice: type: tts.generate dependsOn: [scripts, persona] foreach: scripts.items params: providerPreference: ["cartesia", "elevenlabs", "openai"] voicePolicy: "synthetic_or_owned_only" actorImage: type: image.generatePersona dependsOn: [persona] foreach: persona.items params: providerPreference: ["gemini", "openai", "jimeng"] captionSafeComposition: true talkingHead: type: lipsync.generate dependsOn: [actorImage, voice] foreach: voice.items params: providerPreference: ["fal.musetalk", "replicate.wav2lip", "local.musetalk"] fallback: "static_talking_head_with_audio" brollPrompts: type: broll.promptPack dependsOn: [product, scripts] params: countPerVariant: 2 noReadableTextInModel: true broll: type: video.i2vOrT2v dependsOn: [brollPrompts, product] foreach: brollPrompts.items params: providerPreference: ["jimeng", "gemini.veo", "kling", "fal.wan"] durationSec: 5 captions: type: captions.align dependsOn: [voice] params: providerPreference: ["openai.transcribe", "whisper.local"] style: "ugc-bold-bottom" render: type: render.remotion dependsOn: [talkingHead, broll, captions, product] params: template: "vertical-ugc-v0" layers: - "{{talkingHead}}" - "{{broll}}" - "{{captions}}" - "{{productOverlay}}" analyze: type: analyze.creative dependsOn: [render] params: rubric: ["hook", "clarity", "scroll_stop", "caption_safety", "product_visibility"] 2. Model/API menu Current high-level reality: OpenAI and Google both expose strong image/video/audio capabilities, but Google Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0/O1, Runway Aleph, Seedance, Wan, HunyuanVideo, and LTX are the more relevant moving pieces for this particular Arcads-like system. Google’s Veo 3.1 docs emphasize native synchronized audio and reference-image controls; Runway’s API docs now advertise Aleph 2.0 for editing existing videos with text prompts and keyframe images; Kling’s docs describe O1 as a multimodal video editor for adding/modifying/removing subjects/backgrounds; Wan/VACE/Hunyuan/LTX are the main open/local candidates. Current OpenAI API docs list image models including gpt-image-2, speech models such as GPT‑4o Transcribe and GPT‑4o mini TTS, and Sora pricing/models, but Sora has the deprecation/shutdown caveat above. Use OpenAI strongly for LLM, image, TTS/ASR; use Sora only behind a provider flag. OpenAI Developers+4OpenAI Developers+4OpenAI Developers+4 Google/Gemini. Use Gemini/Nano Banana for character/product image work, and Veo 3.1 for high-quality hero B-roll or reference-image video. The docs currently describe Nano Banana image generation/editing and Veo 3.1 reference-image video generation. Google AI for Developers+1 Anthropic. Use Claude for decomposition, script taste, format extraction, and critique. Anthropic’s docs emphasize prompt caching as a way to reduce repetitive prompt cost/latency, which matters for batch creative generation. Claude Platform Fal/Replicate. Use these as rapid integration layers for model exploration. Fal advertises 1,000+ production-ready image/video/audio/3D model APIs; Replicate’s video collections expose many text-to-video and image-to-video models, including Kling/Wan/Luma-style endpoints. Fal.ai+2Replicate+2 Kling. Strong for product/ad B-roll, start/end frame workflows, O1 editing, and multi-shot experiments. Kling’s current docs describe Kling Video 3.0 and O1 editing, including multimodal add/modify/remove workflows. Kling AI+2Kling AI+2 Runway. Best fit is v2v/editing and high-end creative transformations, especially Aleph. The official API docs now say Aleph 2.0 can edit existing videos with prompts and keyframe images. Runway API Seedance/Dreamina/Jimeng. Very relevant because you already have a Jimeng client. ByteDance’s Seedream image docs describe unified generation/editing and reference consistency; Seedance 2.0 reporting describes multimodal prompts with text/images/video/audio and up to 15-second clips with audio. Use this lane aggressively, but keep it rate-limited, logged, and compliant with account/risk constraints. ByteDance Seed+2ByteDance Seed+2 Open/local video. Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo, and LTX are the main serious candidates. Wan2.2’s repo says it supports text-to-video and image-to-video at 720p/24fps and can run on consumer-grade GPUs like a 4090; HunyuanVideo has 1.5 and avatar/custom branches; LTX describes open access and high-resolution capabilities. Your RTX 3090 is likely more “experimentation/draft/local control” than immediate production unless you are willing to spend time on ComfyUI setup. GitHub+3GitHub+3GitHub+3 Lipsync/open talking head. MuseTalk is currently the best first local/open bet for lipsync; its repo describes real-time high-quality audio-driven lip-sync. Wav2Lip and SadTalker are older but useful fallbacks; SadTalker is specifically audio-driven single-image talking face generation. arXiv+3GitHub+3GitHub+3 Audio. ElevenLabs remains the quality default for synthetic voices and consented cloning; its docs expose TTS, STT, voice cloning, and official SDKs. Cartesia is attractive for fast, controllable TTS; its docs currently show Sonic 3.5 as generally available and voice cloning through the API/playground. Cartesia Docs+4ElevenLabs+4ElevenLabs+4 Captions/segmentation. Whisper/faster-whisper are the cheap/local ASR path; SAM 2/SAM 3, BiRefNet, RMBG, and rembg are the segmentation/background-removal path. Whisper is documented as multilingual ASR/translation; faster-whisper reimplements Whisper with CTranslate2 for faster/lower-memory inference; Meta’s SAM 2 docs describe promptable image/video segmentation. The point is to prove the graph/layer system.
